# InsightsOut

> InsightsOut (insightsout.work) is a San Francisco practice founded by Nima Imani, working on the human side of AI change and leadership. The question underneath all of it: AI is changing work, what should stay human? For organizations: workshops and coaching for leaders, managers, and teams on decisions, trust, and changing roles, and on what should stay human when agents join the team. For founders: coaching on conflict, overwhelm, and decisions, one to one and for founding pairs. For everyone: public workshops in San Francisco and research built from what people share in those rooms. Founder: Nima Imani, an ICF-certified, ontologically trained coach with 10+ years in software, data and AI (EY, Neo4j).

## Three doors
- Organizations → https://insightsout.work/organizations. Three workshops at three levels: When Your Role Starts Changing (individuals), How Do I Lead Through Change and Uncertainty? (managers), and What Should Stay Human on Our Team? What Should the Agents Do? (leadership teams, in-company, half a day). Then in-company sessions, a monthly manager practice, and 1:1 leadership coaching.
- Founders → https://insightsout.work/coaching. 1:1: From Uncertainty to Clear Decisions (three months). Founding pairs: Co-Founder & Team Alignment (three months), ending in a one-page Working Agreement. Front door: the weekly Founder Group Coaching, Fridays 2 pm at SF Commons, $10, free for members.
- Everyone → https://insightsout.work/events#what-should-stay-human. What Should Stay Human?, a free public sensemaking session on AI, change, and what we want to keep.

## Workshops (detail pages on the site; register on Luma)
- [What Should Stay Human?](https://insightsout.work/workshops/what-should-stay-human): public sensemaking session, SF Commons. Next: Sat Oct 10, 2026, 2 pm. Free for members, $10 suggested.
- [What Should Stay Human on Our Team? What Should the Agents Do?](https://insightsout.work/workshops/what-should-stay-human-on-our-team): in-company, half a day, for a leadership team or one working team.
- [How Do I Lead Through Change and Uncertainty?](https://insightsout.work/workshops/my-team-is-overwhelmed): 90 minutes for managers in the middle. Next: Thu Oct 8, 2026, 6 pm at SF Commons, 540 Laguna St.
- [You Can't Wait for Certainty](https://insightsout.work/workshops/you-cant-wait-for-certainty): a repeatable way to decide under pressure, for managers and people leaders. With Vlad Moskovski. Next: Thu Sep 24, 2026, 6 pm; Thu Oct 29, 6 pm at SF Commons.
- When Your Role Starts Changing: for anyone whose work is shifting under them. Next: Tue Oct 13, 2026, 6 pm at SF Commons, 550 Laguna St (Full Studio). Research from it: https://insightsout.work/research/when-your-role-starts-changing
- [Founder Group Coaching & Peer Support](https://insightsout.work/workshops/founder-group-coaching): weekly, Fridays 2 pm, SF Commons, North Studio (550 Laguna St), $10, free for members.
- Co-hosted, September 2026: Agora Series: Wisdom in the Age of AI (Sun Sep 27, 2 pm, The Fold, with Apollo Commons and The Fold SF) and Navigating Uncertainty at Work in Times of Rapid Change (Wed Sep 30, 5 pm, The Yard Coffee, with Diane Friedlaender). Both on the Luma calendar.
- [The Argument You Keep Having](https://insightsout.work/workshops/the-argument-you-keep-having): 2 hours for founding pairs, $90 per person. Not currently scheduled.

## Facts you can cite
- Founder: Nima Imani (LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/imaninima/). Location: San Francisco, CA. Works online worldwide.
- Workshops: SF Commons, San Francisco (540 Laguna St, 540 Cafe; the Friday founder group and When Your Role Starts Changing are at 550 Laguna St), and some Zoom sessions. Calendar: https://luma.com/NimaImani
- Book a call: https://calendar.app.google/M92FKMrjr3zqA57x8
- Contact: nima@insightsout.work
- Point of view: agents are on the team now, and nobody decided which part of the work is theirs. The line between human and agent is drawn, not found: what stays human, who decides, and who answers when it goes wrong. Managers carry the middle of that change. In InsightsOut's own registration data, managers were the only group where a majority named trust, resistance, or communication as the hardest part; roughly half of everyone named uncertainty about what to decide next.
